reasons: Each rule has a matching test with a clear failure message.
Some checks depend on phrase matching, which is a known limit.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: File setup and sample claim
sections.what: Imports the critic, its challenge types, and the claim payload. Defines one sample claim about analyst hours with one evidence id.
sections.why: Reason not stated beyond use as shared test input.

sections.name: anyio_backend
sections.title: Async test engine selection
sections.what: Selects asyncio as the engine that runs the async tests.
sections.why: Likely reason: async tests need a runner.

sections.name: challenge
sections.title: Sample challenge builder
sections.what: Builds a sample challenge against the current state block, with a chosen struck evidence id and objection text.
sections.why: Reason not stated beyond use as shared test input.

sections.name: coverage
sections.title: Coverage formula copy
sections.what: Computes coverage as one minus e to the power of minus count over three. Used so tests can show that striking evidence lowers coverage.
sections.why: The docstring says it is used to show that a strike actually moves confidence.
sections.watch_out: The formula is copied here, so if the real formula changes, these tests will not notice.

sections.name: TestHappyPath
sections.title: Happy path checks
sections.what: Checks the critic returns a verdict containing challenges, routes to the defensible model tier, and treats an empty challenge list as a valid result with no strikes.
sections.why: The docstring says the critic is where overclaiming is caught, so it gets the stronger model.

sections.name: TestItCanForceADowngrade
sections.title: Critic can force a downgrade
sections.what: Checks a challenge's struck evidence becomes a removable id in the verdict. Strikes are grouped per block. Striking evidence lowers coverage. An objection with no strike is allowed.
sections.why: The docstring says the downgrade comes from removing evidence, not from a stated number.

sections.name: TestItCannotSetConfidence
sections.title: Critic cannot set confidence
sections.what: Checks confidence and score fields are absent from the critic output and challenge types. Also checks the challenge contract has no confidence field, and the task forbids stating confidence.
sections.why: Reason stated in the test names: confidence is computed elsewhere from evidence coverage.
sections.watch_out: Adding a score field would let the critic set confidence directly.

sections.name: TestItCannotRewrite
sections.title: Critic cannot rewrite claims
sections.what: Checks there is no replacement or rewrite field. Objections that contain a corrected figure or corrected version are refused, while plain objections pass. Also checks the task forbids repair.
sections.why: Reason stated in the test names: the critic objects and does not fix.
sections.watch_out: The refusal relies on phrase matching, so reworded corrections may pass.

sections.name: TestUpheldIsNotTheCriticsToSet
sections.title: Critic cannot uphold its own objections
sections.what: Checks every challenge comes back with the upheld flag set to false. Also checks the model is never offered that field.
sections.why: The docstring says a critic that could uphold its own challenge would be deciding, not reviewing.

sections.name: TestFailurePaths
sections.title: Failure path checks
sections.what: Checks a strike on evidence outside the pack is rejected with the id named. A bad strike is retried once, and accepted if the retry is valid. An unknown block name cannot be used.
sections.why: Reason not stated beyond the test names.
sections.watch_out: Only one retry happens, so a second bad answer fails the run.

summary: A set of tests that checks the red team critic can lower confidence only by striking evidence, and cannot set confidence, rewrite claims or uphold its own objections.
purpose: Proves the critic reviews claims and does not decide or repair them.
why: The docstring says the critic lowers confidence by striking evidence, never by asserting a number. The rest of the file follows that rule.
how: Pytest loads the file. A fake model returns scripted challenges. Each test runs the critic and checks one rule, such as struck evidence, refused rewrites, or the upheld flag.
inputs: A fake model client, a sample claim about analyst hours, the process brief, and a run context with evidence.
outputs: Pass or fail results for each test. Nothing is written to disk.
risks: Phrase checks are a limited filter. The coverage formula is copied into the tests, so a change to the real formula is not caught here.
debug: If a strike test fails, check the critic's evidence handling and the run context evidence count. If a rewrite check fails, look at the objection text the fake model returned.
